verify.notes: IMPORTANT: this gate's own verdict, on its own criteria, was NOT PASSED — 05-verification.v8.md §11 states this explicitly. Status is recorded here as "passed" only because of the product-owner override logged below (overrides[0]), not because the gate's acceptance criteria were met. Read 05-verification.v8.md in full before treating this branch as verified; do not infer from status=passed alone that every finding was closed. Eight verify passes were run against this branch (v1-v8, one per remediation cycle); the full chain is preserved in pdlc/arsene-cms/ and pdlc/arsene-cms/verify/ and indexed in the log below. Findings genuinely and fully closed by v8, confirmed by independent adversarial testing: the discard route's core mechanism (CAS race, grant boundary, draft-lock check), M-V7-02 (render cover-blanking), and the practical effect of L-V7-01 (cover uniqueness) on a freshly-migrated database. Findings NOT closed, and the subject of the override: (1) migration 0005 cannot apply to a database already holding duplicate ready-cover rows, a state proven reachable through ordinary concurrent use with no attacker — 05-verification.v8.md §4; (2) the discard route has no src/api/client.ts method and no contract declaration, so the product's own editor SPA cannot currently call the route this whole cycle exists to provide — 05-verification.v8.md §5. Also open, not blocking: L-V8-01 (discard route has no rate limit or audit trail), L-V8-02 (discard permanently orphans the file in Supabase Storage), plus the standing backlog carried since v3-v7 (L-V7-02 updated_at forgeable, I-V7-01 missing CHECK constraint, L-V6-01 CDN_ORIGIN validation, L-V6-03 transient slug race, N5/N5b, N2, idempotency store TTL/writer_id scoping). Counter-metric (writer adoption) remains honestly uncomputable from any event this build emits, unchanged since the architecture gate; required events draft_started/article_published both confirmed emitted correctly via the real primary path across every one of the eight verify passes' instrumentation proofs, most recently §10 of 05-verification.v8.md.

pipeline.notes: Status upgraded from "partial" to "passed": the finding v1 raised (API server built for Node's http.createServer/node:child_process, but ADR-0001 named Supabase Edge Functions/Deno) is closed. Per explicit product-owner instruction, src/api/router.ts was refactored so route()/dispatch()/every handler-dependency builder operates on the standard Fetch API (Request in, Response out) rather than Node's http types, with two thin adapters on top: the existing Node one (startHttpServer, unchanged behaviour, same exported name/ServerOptions shape the test suite's seam expects - all 227 pre-existing tests pass unchanged, zero test edits) and a new real Deno one (supabase/functions/arsene-api/index.ts, a genuine Deno.serve handler). A real regression was found and fixed during the port: the WHATWG Fetch spec forbids constructing a Request with method TRACE/TRACK/CONNECT, which the existing Schemathesis contract suite's TRACE case caught immediately once the Node adapter was rebuilt on a real Request object - fixed by threading the real wire method through route() explicitly rather than trusting request.method, confirmed fixed under both adapters. The dev/test-only Lambda simulation (convert(), which needs real sharp, a native addon Deno cannot load) is wired only by the Node adapter; its import of lambdaHandler.ts was changed from static to a lazy, non-literal dynamic import specifically so importing route()/buildCtx() from router.ts - which the Deno entry point does - never pulls sharp into the Edge Function's module graph, confirmed empirically with disposable spike files before relying on it (10-pipeline.v2.md §3). Rehearsed for real: deno check and deno run against real local Postgres, real curl/raw-socket HTTP driving every route (auth success/failure, 404/405/413, the TRACE fix, the full ADR-0004 upload+callback loop confirming sharp is genuinely never invoked, and a real measured 408 timeout at 1.502s against a configured 1500ms). Six new permanent automated tests (tests/e2e/deployedDenoRuntime.test.ts, via new tests/support/denoServer.ts) spawn a genuine deno run child process against real Testcontainers Postgres over real HTTP, mirroring deployedAuthBoundary.test.ts's pattern for the Node boundary - full suite is now 233/233, zero regressions. deploy.yml/rollback.yml's deploy-api-server/redeploy-api-server jobs now run real `supabase functions deploy` (current docs' recommended supabase/setup-cli@v1 pattern) instead of a loudly-failing stub; both test jobs gained a denoland/setup-deno@v2 step so the new suite can run in CI. NOT rehearsed: the actual `supabase functions deploy` round-trip against the real linked project (dmytkubjxwwwkroutvdu) - consistent with v1's own local-only rehearsal and this branch's standing practice of not touching a real/paid/shared account without explicit confirmation first; CLI syntax is sourced from current docs but not itself executed live. A new, disclosed, out-of-scope finding surfaced while reading current docs: Supabase's docs now describe the shared HS256 JWT-secret model auth.ts verifies against (SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET) as the legacy system, 'no longer recommended, available for backward compatibility', superseded by a newer Signing keys system. Not a regression, not fixed here, not blocking - recorded in 10-pipeline.v2.md §4 for a future gate to decide. Unchanged from v1: no Cloudflare Pages/public-site deployable artifact exists anywhere in this repo; the migration-0005 one-way-door reconciliation is still manual, not automated; state.json's overrides[0] accepted-risk record is untouched.

dashboard.notes: Built the data adapter and the dashboard. Adapter: GET /internal/metrics/time-to-publish, a new route on the existing Edge Function (not PostgREST - telemetry_events has RLS enabled with zero policies, and this app uses no Data API access anywhere else either), guarded by a new DASHBOARD_READ_SECRET shared secret checked from headers alone, never a writer JWT. Returns raw {published_at, minutes} samples (never writer_id/article_id) plus a counter-metric count of distinct active writers in the last 30 days (never a list). 10 new tests (unit + real-DB + real-spawned-route), 244/244 total, zero regressions. dashboard/index.html: single self-contained static file, no framework/build step, base URL and secret entered by the viewer and stored in localStorage (never baked into the file). Rehearsed for real: a real serverMain.ts process against real seeded Postgres answered the real endpoint correctly (median 9 min from 3 real samples, 2 active writers); the dashboard's client-side median/bucketing logic was verified against that exact real payload in Node. NOT verified: the page actually rendering in a browser - no Chrome extension connected and no headless-browser tooling (playwright/puppeteer/jsdom) installed in this environment; disclosed plainly in 11-dashboard.v1.md §3 rather than claimed as tested. Baseline captured: Pam's self-reported ~50min estimate is unchanged and still the only baseline available - zero real articles have been published in production, so 'current' cannot be measured yet (state.json's success.metrics[0].current now says so explicitly rather than showing a fabricated number). Counter-metric similarly not yet measurable (0 real writers).

release.notes: Product owner approved v0.2.0 in chat ('Approve v0.2.0', no scoping) after reviewing the compact release summary: what ships, verification results (244/244, real computed metric from verify v1/v8), baseline captured (Pam's ~50min estimate, current not yet measurable), rollback mechanism + measured times, one-way doors, and residual risks. Re-checking the rollback at this gate (per this gate's own 'things change between gates' instruction) surfaced a real finding: v0.1.0 is not a safe rollback target for the API server since it predates the Deno port and cannot run on the real Edge Function target at all - this is the first real deploy this product has ever attempted, so there is no previously-deployed good version to fall back to. The stale v0.1.0 tag (pointing at a commit two features behind HEAD) was not reused; v0.2.0 was cut fresh. No new migrations this release, so no new one-way doors. NOT DEPLOYED: this repository has no git remote configured (confirmed via git remote -v), so .github/workflows/deploy.yml cannot run - there is nothing to push the tag to. The approval covers the release content; a real deploy still needs a remote, GitHub repo secrets (SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN, SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF, SUPABASE_DB_URL), and the Edge Function's own runtime secrets set via `supabase secrets set` - none of which this or any prior session has had access to configure. See APPROVAL.md and RELEASE-EVIDENCE.md for the full record.

overrides.reason: After eight red/green/verify remediation cycles (2026-08-11 through 2026-08-20), verify v8 (05-verification.v8.md) found the underlying server-side security and correctness work fully sound under independent adversarial testing — the new discard route's safety argument, CAS race handling, and grant boundary all survived from-scratch adversarial re-derivation by two independent verify agents, and no High-severity finding exists anywhere in the current state. What remained open were two Medium findings about reach rather than correctness: (1) migration 0005's cover-uniqueness index cannot apply to a database already holding the duplicate-cover state a prior finding (L-V7-01) proved reachable through ordinary use; (2) the new recovery route has no client method or contract declaration, so the product's own editor SPA cannot call it yet. Product owner reviewed this specific finding set and decided to ship as-is, accepting both as known, tracked limitations rather than continuing remediation before shipping.

accepted_findings.summary: Migration 0005 (partial unique index on article_images enforcing one ready cover per article) aborts with a Postgres uniqueness-violation error if applied to a database that already holds duplicate ready-cover rows on one article — a state 05-verification.v7.md §6 (L-V7-01) proved reachable through ordinary concurrent cover uploads, no attacker required. No test in the suite can catch this because every test database starts empty (tests/support/pg.ts). Recommended fix (not yet applied): a pre-flight step in the migration demoting all but the most-recently-created ready cover on each article before creating the index, plus a red-gate test that migrates a database seeded with the duplicate state rather than only an empty one.
accepted_findings.risk_if_unaddressed: If this branch is ever deployed to a database that has already exhibited the L-V7-01 duplicate-cover state, the migration will fail loudly (blocking the deploy, requiring manual data surgery) under a stop-on-error runner, or may silently never create the index under a more tolerant one — in which case cover uniqueness is not actually enforced in that environment despite the code and tests suggesting it is.

accepted_findings.summary: The DELETE /v1/articles/{id}/images/{id} discard route (src/api/discardImage.ts), the writer-facing recovery mechanism this entire eighth remediation cycle exists to build, has no method on src/api/client.ts and is documented in contracts/openapi.yaml as prose only, not a declared path item. The server-side capability is complete, correct, and thoroughly verified (see verify §2); nothing in the current codebase lets the actual editor SPA construct a request to it.
accepted_findings.risk_if_unaddressed: A writer whose article becomes permanently stuck (per the two routes documented in 05-verification.v7.md §4) has no way to recover through the actual product UI until a client method and contract declaration are added — only a direct HTTP request (e.g. via curl or a future SPA release) can currently invoke the fix.

not_accepted_as_blocking_but_tracked: L-V8-01: the discard route has no rate limit and writes no telemetry/audit record (pdlc/arsene-cms/05-verification.v8.md §6)

Re-checking rollback at this gate surfaced a real finding: v0.1.0 predates the Deno port and cannot run on the real Edge Function target, so it is not a safe rollback destination - this is the first real deploy ever attempted, so there is no previously-deployed good version to fall back to. Real deploy attempted after the release-gate approval: git remote created (github.com/lionelleboiteux/arsene-cms), v0.1.0/v0.2.0 tags pushed, SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN/PROJECT_REF/DB_URL secrets added. First real workflow_dispatch run (32627039526): Edge Function deploy SUCCEEDED for the first time ever; Postgres migration deploy failed on a malformed connection string (unencoded special character in the password shifted psql's URI parsing) - fixed by re-setting the secret. Second run (32627585524): the test gate itself failed for a real reason, not flakiness - Schemathesis fuzzing POST /v1/articles against the exact code being deployed found a title containing a NUL byte crashed the request with a raw 500. Root cause: Postgres text columns reject any value containing a NUL byte (error 22021), and nothing validated against it before repo.ts's insert. Fixed in src/api/router.ts by rejecting a NUL byte in every free-text field CreateDraftBody/PublishBody accept, at the same Zod-validation layer that already rejects other malformed input. Confirmed against a real server (500 to 400); regression-tested (tests/e2e/nulByteValidation.test.ts, 4 new tests); full suite re-run three extra times with fresh random fuzz seeds, all green; 248/248 total. Recorded as v0.2.1 in CHANGELOG.md. Current live state: the Edge Function is deployed running v0.2.0's code (with the bug); migrations were never applied to the real project; v0.2.1 is fixed locally but not yet tagged, pushed or deployed. Full detail in RELEASE-EVIDENCE.md.

v0.2.1 tagged and pushed; deploy triggered. A major finding surfaced mid-deploy: mcp__supabase__list_tables revealed SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF/SUPABASE_DB_URL were pointed at the Supabase project shared with the sibling pronos product - a live production database (48 players, 956 predictions, 1124 telemetry events) with its own leagues and telemetry_events tables of entirely different shape than Arsene's, an unresolvable name collision. A writers table and an empty _migrations_applied were also found already present, meaning an earlier partial migration attempt had run against this same shared project before this pipeline existed. Investigation was read-only; nothing was modified. Product owner created a new, dedicated Supabase project (within the Free plan's two-project allowance) and re-pointed the three secrets at it. After resolving a wrong database password (confirmed independently via a direct local psql connection with the value shared in chat - recommended resetting it since it had been pasted into the conversation) and two transient new-project-provisioning failures (404 on functions list, pooler tenant not found), the sixth real workflow_dispatch run (32639503102, 2026-08-23T12:31Z) succeeded completely: test suite (2m7s), Edge Function deploy (21s, confirmed via its own 'Deployed Functions on project' output), and all five Postgres migrations applied in order for the first time against the real dedicated database (35s, 'migrations up to date'). This is the first fully successful production deploy of Arsene. Remaining: the Edge Function's own runtime secrets (SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET, IMAGE_CALLBACK_SECRET, CDN_ORIGIN, WRITER_TOKEN, WRITER_ID, DASHBOARD_READ_SECRET) still need to be set via `supabase secrets set` on the new project - not automated by CI, by design - before the deployed function will answer real requests instead of failing closed. Full sequence in RELEASE-EVIDENCE.md.

Found while working out how to actually reach the deployed function: Supabase's platform-level verify_jwt gateway check (on by default) inspects Authorization on every request before the function runs and requires a genuine Supabase JWT there. POST /internal/images/{id}/status and GET /internal/metrics/time-to-publish never send an Authorization header at all (they use their own shared-secret headers), so the platform would reject both with a 401 before router.ts's own already-correct auth logic ever ran. Not catchable by any existing test - neither the Node adapter nor local `deno run` has this extra gateway layer, it only exists on the real managed platform, the same class of gap the whole Deno-port effort exists to catch. Fixed by adding supabase/config.toml with [functions.arsene-api] verify_jwt = false, Supabase's documented pattern for functions mixing JWT and non-JWT callers - confirmed via current docs this setting applies to real deploys, not just local `functions serve`. router.ts's own route() already gates every request regardless, so this removes a redundant, actively-breaking platform check without removing any real protection. Recorded as v0.2.2 in CHANGELOG.md. Requires a redeploy to take effect on the already-deployed function.
